context_title:
Build a complete, production-grade, standalone frontend UI system for a chat interface header action bar in such a way that the final result precisely matches the visual world of the existing website. The design must be built from the provided tokens and must rely on the blue brand accent while preserving the dark base surface, white/faded text colors, glass-like translucent layers, subtle blurs, rounded shapes, and compact icon-centric controls. The implementation must include all necessary files, components, styles, state management, responsive logic, and accessibility behavior in fully complete, deployable code.

The entire system must be built on a central design token architecture. Tokens must be the only source of all visual values: colors, typography, spacing, border radii, icon sizes, motion values, and shadows must all be derived from tokens. Treat the following token set as the base and map all UI values from it: --color-surface-base: #000000, --color-foreground-text: #f5f5f7, --color-pure-white: #ffffff, --color-pure-white-accent: #ffffff, --color-near-black-surface: #09090f, --color-near-black-deep: #09090f, --color-brand-blue: #0000ff. The typography scale must match the provided tokens exactly: Body Default 16px/400, Body Secondary 15px/400, Label Small 11px/400, Label Medium Semibold 13.5px/500, Nav Title 15px/600, Caption Uppercase 11px/600/0.5px letter spacing, Message Body 13px/400/19.5px line-height, Display Heading 20px/600, Body Readable 16px/400/23.2px line-height. The spacing tokens must be used exactly: space-2 2px, space-3 3px, space-4 4px, space-5 5px, space-6 6px, space-7 7px, space-8 8px, space-9 9px, space-10 10px, space-11 11px, space-12 12px, space-13 13px, space-14 14px, space-16 16px, space-17 17px, space-20 20px, space-48 48px. The border radius tokens must be: radius-message-bubble 18px, radius-input 16px, radius-button 23px. The entire UI must work in both dark and light mode; color switching must happen exclusively through token value replacement without changing component logic.

Create a reusable horizontal action bar container that sits in the chat header and follows the existing glassmorphism visual language of the website. The container must be a flex row that centers all child elements vertically and horizontally, and must appear with a subtle translucent background, blur effect, faint border, and radius-button rounding. The surface must match the existing dark base color and blue accent system so that the container appears as if it belongs to the same design system. Padding, border, background, inset highlight, and shadow values must all come from tokens.

Define explicit responsive breakpoints and separate behavior for each. xs is 0–479px, sm is 480–767px, md is 768–1023px, lg is 1024px and above. In xs and sm views, icon size must be icon.sm (16px), spacing between controls must be space-1 or the closest minimal token, the Share control must be hidden, and minimum touch target must be at least 36px. In md view, icon size must be icon.md (20px), spacing must be space-2, all controls must be visible, and minimum touch target must be at least 40px. In lg view, also use icon.md (20px), spacing must be space-3, all controls must remain visible, minimum touch target must be at least 44px, and hover feedback must be stronger while still subtle. When a control is hidden, the layout must not break, must not reflow unstably, and the group’s visual centering must remain fixed.

Render four controls in strict left-to-right order: New chat, Share chat, More options, Files and sources. Each control must be a semantic <button> with a square hit area, centered icon, and state styling consistent with the website’s current button system. The base state must use surface.base or its equivalent token surface value, hover must use surface.hover, active must use surface.active, all with short motion.fast transitions. Button size, padding, border radius, and shadow must align with the existing rounded glass UI elements.

The New chat control must always be visible and must navigate to the chat start view. Its aria label must be exactly Új csevegés. The Share chat control must open the sharing flow, its aria label must be Csevegés megosztása, and it must be hidden on xs and sm breakpoints and visible from md upward. The More options control must open a contextual menu and implement proper menu semantics: aria-haspopup="menu", dynamic aria-expanded, and precise open/close state handling. The Files and sources control must open a panel or modal for files and sources, must use aria-haspopup="dialog", must have dynamic aria-expanded and/or aria-pressed state, and must visually indicate its active state when open.

Icons must be inline SVGs or equivalent components, must inherit text color, and must always be centered inside the button. Icon size must follow breakpoints: 16px for xs/sm, 20px for md/lg. Icons and buttons must maintain the same visual quality in hover, focus, and active states as the rest of the site. Do not use foreign icon styles, mismatched stroke weights, or any iconography that does not match the current blue-accent interface.

Ensure full accessibility. Every control must be keyboard accessible with a logical focus order. Every interactive element must have a stable and meaningful ARIA label. Focus state must be visibly indicated using focus.ring and shadow.focus tokens, and focus indication must never be removed without replacement. Menu and dialog triggers must reflect open/closed state in real time. Disabled state must be handled correctly with reduced opacity and pointer blocking. Focus, hover, active, and expanded states must be deterministic, predictable, and explicitly managed.

Interaction logic must be consistent: hover uses surface.hover, active uses surface.active, focus uses focus.ring plus shadow.focus, and transitions must use motion.fast. All state changes must be explicit and must not rely on implicit or uncertain DOM behavior. The user experience must be precise, clean, and fully aligned with the existing website’s blue, dark, translucent visual character.

The code must be structured modularly with strict separation of concerns. A separate layer must exist for the token system and theme switching, a base primitive layer for button and icon wrappers, a dedicated component for the conversation header action bar, a separate state management layer for menu and dialog logic, a responsive layer for breakpoint handling, and an accessibility layer for ARIA state management. The implementation must be complete, clean, well-structured, and maintainable.

The output must include all required source files, token implementation, components, state management, responsive styling system, accessibility logic, and theme switching mechanism. No placeholders, mocks, pseudo-code, dummy data, fake behavior, or incomplete modules are allowed. The system must be fully functional, deployable, and 100% consistent across all breakpoints, all themes, and all interaction states, and must perfectly match the existing website design.


the frontend must be contained in a single index.html file
Send back the complete code with all the fixes. Fix each of the listed errors one by one, making sure to actually correct them so that there are 0 errors remaining. Keep the original imports, since the files exist. Write out every single character; do not abbreviate anything. Fix every error. There must be exactly one file. Do not write anything else; just output the complete code, and it must not contain any comments. Never, under any circumstances, use simplified, substitute, dummy, simulated, or fake code. Write the entire file as complete, unabridged, production-ready code in a single code block. It must be 100% error-free, a complete, error-free file, and must be submitted as a downloadable file. These requirements are mandatory and must be strictly adhered to. If no list of errors is provided, you must find all the errors and fix them. If there were comments in the original code, delete them. And most importantly: YOU MUST NEVER SIMPLIFY!
